review_notes: The file has one declaration, `nb095SplitAlpha0000`. It is a very large generated term of type `TAlphaWff ...`. It builds an alpha-equivalence certificate between two class-theory formulas from the `TAlphaWff`, `TAlphaClass` and `TAlphaVar` constructors. These relation types and the `Class`/`Wff`/`synC*` syntax are defined in the project's own earlier files. The file itself introduces no new type, structure or definition of a concept. I judged that the alpha-equivalence relation for this custom set-theory syntax does not match anything in Mathlib, Batteries or core. Mathlib's first-order `BoundedFormula` uses de Bruijn indices and so has no alpha-equivalence to mirror. I did not search the Mathlib sources for it. I did not read the upstream project files that define the `TAlpha*` types. The lines `Nat.ne_of_lt (mem_lt_freshVar ...)` and `freshVar_injective` are project-specific freshness lemmas. They are proof-term repetition, not a competing concept, and the rubric excludes that. I found no justified finding.
